questions.stem: What frequency band do EPIRBs and PLBs use?
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 200 defines both as operating in the 406 MHz band.

questions.stem: What does a radar SART do?
options: Responds to a rescuer's 9 GHz X-band radar so survivors can be pinpointed
questions.explanation: A SART is a locating device, a secondary device; the EPIRB is the primary alert.

questions.stem: How does a radar SART appear on a rescuer's radar within about 8 nautical miles?
options: As a line of 12 dots, becoming arcs then circles within about 1 nm
questions.explanation: Wikipedia describes 12 dots about 0.64 nm apart, with arcs and circles close in.

questions.stem: A float-free EPIRB is required on:
options: a vessel on a near coastal voyage Class 1 or an unlimited voyage
a vessel in sheltered waters only
questions.explanation: Section 209(1)(a); also a vessel over 12 m on an inland or Class 2 voyage.

questions.stem: A 10 m vessel on a near coastal Class 2 voyage may carry which of these instead of a float-free EPIRB?
options: A manual EPIRB or a PLB
questions.explanation: Section 209(3) lets a vessel of 12 m or less on Class 2 or inland carry a float-free EPIRB, manual EPIRB, PLB, or (under 8 m, A1 only) a waterproof DSC handheld.

questions.stem: Where must a manual EPIRB, PLB or DSC handheld used under s. 209(3) be kept?
options: Worn by the person in charge of the navigational watch, or stowed ready for abandonment

questions.stem: How soon must a change be entered in the Canadian Beacon Registry?
How often must an EPIRB, PLB or SART be inspected and tested by a radio operator?
options: On installation and at least every six months
questions.explanation: Section 239 (except beacons stowed in an inflatable life raft).

questions.stem: Which beacon is the primary alert device and which is secondary?
options: EPIRB is primary; SART is secondary
SART is primary; EPIRB is secondary
questions.explanation: The EPIRB alerts the rescue system; the SART helps rescuers locate survivors.

questions.stem: What does s. 208 require for one of the SARTs on board?
options: It must be sealed in the raft
It must be stowed so it is readily accessible for immediate use on board

questions.stem: An EPIRB battery must be replaced when:
options: after use in an emergency, after inadvertent activation, as a test requires, or by its expiry date

questions.stem: An EPIRB sends a 406 MHz signal to satellites. What is its 121.5 MHz signal for?
options: A homing signal for the final approach
questions.explanation: Jotron describes 406 MHz for the distress signal and 121.5 MHz for homing.

questions.stem: Which is a requirement for a float-free EPIRB under s. 209(2)?
options: It must float free if the vessel sinks and be able to be released by hand and carried into a survival craft
It must be bolted to the mast
It must be switched off at sea
It must be stowed in the engine room
questions.explanation: Section 209(2)(a) to (c) also requires it to be readily accessible near the navigating position unless it can be activated remotely from there.
